notes:
ACCURACY: 25 sampled with random.seed(7) / random.sample over the 282 harvest brands; all seven source pages re-fetched raw (Parallel web_fetch full_content; summaries in AUDIT_G2_tmp/raw/). All 25 names are shown on their src pages. 1 wrong: Loveday Belgravia (WhatHouse 2025 bronze retirement developer) is a luxury nursing/residential care home (Loveday & Co, care fees from GBP 4,500/week), a care service, not property bought or owned. 2 'partly': Davidsons Developments and Amethyst Homes rest on newbuildrankings.com.
HBF FAITHFULNESS (caveat checked): newbuildrankings.com does NOT reproduce HBF's 2026 Star Ratings faithfully. HBF's own 2026 brochure (hbf.co.uk/documents/15516/...brochure_4.pdf, fetched) says 2026 stars are a composite of four 8-week and 9-month satisfaction scores (scheme reviewed by Ipsos; 5 stars needs >= 4.15), whereas NBR maps stars with the old '90%+ would recommend = 5 star' rule on 'rolling 12-month' data. NBR omits Barratt Redrow (12,411 surveyed) and Hill Group (362), lists Lovell, Rectory Homes (10 surveyed), Avant Homes, McCarthy Stone and Untypical that are absent from HBF's 2026 table, and shifts sample sizes for Churchill, Crest Nicholson, Croudace and Cavanna. The star column in HBF's PDF is graphic, so the 5-star list itself cannot be read from text. Fix: re-source the 20 surviving NBR rows to the HBF brochure (all 20 appear there, Rose Builders as 'Rose Builder', Davidsons as 'Davidsons Homes', Cala as 'CALA Group'), drop the '5-star band' wording, and tier them cultural (a buyer survey is standing, not a test). Rectory Homes dropped. Four HBF-table builders the harvest missed are added (Denbury, Homes by Honey - the harvest's 'unclear' row is spelled so by HBF itself -, Cavanna, Stancliffe).
WHATHOUSE: the 2025 page thanks the judges (juried = quality). Winners checked for supplier/architect/agent: the harvest correctly skipped sponsors (LAUFEN, Roca, Blum, Beko, Mitsubishi Electric etc.). Non-homebuilder winners kept by the harvest: Loveday Belgravia (care home, drop), Dolphin Square (a single rental block, drop), PLATFORM_ and Dandara Living and Quintain (build-to-rent landlords; scope query: renting is not buying/owning), Elysian Residences and Mayfield Villages (retirement villages; keep if units are sold). Housebuilder Awards 2025 rows were not re-fetched (not in sample): verifier should check Excelsior Land and Quinn Estates (possibly land promoters rather than homebuilders).
DUPLICATES to merge: Vistry / Vistry Group; Cala Group / Cala Homes (HBF: CALA Group); Hill Holdings / The Hill Group (HBF: Hill Group); Strata / Strata Homes (HBF: Strata Group); Latimer / Latimer by Clarion Housing Group; Spitfire Homes / Spitfire Bespoke Homes; Robertson Residential / Robertson Homes; Quintain / Quintain Living; Abbey Developments / Abbey New Homes; St Modwen Homes is a Miller Homes brand since Feb 2025; St James and St George are Berkeley Group brands; Kebbell Homes (WhatHouse) = Kebbell Development (HBF); Morris Homes = Morris Homes Group (HBF); Churchill Living = Churchill Retirement Living (HBF); Emaar Hospitality is the Emaar Properties hospitality arm; Capri Holdings folds into Versace.
BRANDED RESIDENCES / CROSS-TAGS: Savills 2023 (fetched) supports Versace (Versace Residences, 'Capri Holdings (Versace)'), Hyatt (top-10 hotel parent by schemes), Dolce & Gabbana and De Grisogono (debut schemes in the pipeline before 2030: mark as pipeline). All four are the same companies as their register rows, so cross-tag. Added cross-tags from Savills 2020/2023 and Dezeen: Roberto Cavalli, Fendi, Baccarat, Greg Norman, Bulgari, Swarovski, Diesel, Gianfranco Ferré, Porsche Design, Bentley (G1 Bentley Motors, not E3 Bentley), Bugatti, Mercedes-Benz, Muji (Good Design Award houses), Vipp (Vipp Shelter).
HOMONYMS: Barratt Redrow vs Barratt sweets (J8) confirmed different. John Taylor (Monaco estate agent, Worthbury list) was skipped by the harvest because the register has John Taylor (E3, bell foundry): added as 'John Taylor (estate agent)', homonym. Westin (hotels) vs harvest Westin Homes (Texas builder); Regent (hotels) vs register Regent (A1); Sobha Limited (India) vs Sobha Realty (Dubai); Prestige Estates Projects (India) vs register Prestige (G2 park homes); Binet Homes vs register Binet (J7); Daiwa House vs register Daiwa (E2 fishing tackle); Panasonic Homes and Toyota Home must not cross-tag Panasonic/Toyota automatically (separate housebuilding companies, now under Prime Life Technologies); Crest Nicholson, Miller Homes, Ivory Homes, Orbit Homes, Holiday Builders carry full names, but the merge must not fuzzy-match them to Crest (H1), Miller (C1), Ivory (H1), Orbit (B10), Holiday (A1). Sekisui House U.S. is the same group as Sekisui House; Sumitomo Forestry Australia the same as Sumitomo Forestry; Mitsui Home is Mitsui Fudosan group.
BUILDGREENNH LIST: an AI-assisted listicle (site has a 'Generative AI Disclaimer'); its rows are existence-only. Garbled rows dropped (Klaus = K-Haus, Spazio = Spassio/Aito Lapland, Simple Homes links an unrelated site); Claesson Koivisto Rune is an architecture practice. Vitus trades as VitHaus (vithaus.eu).
OMISSIONS ADDED (165 brands): Builder 100 rows the harvest skipped without reason (18; AMH build-to-rent landlord and NeighborWorks nonprofit network left out); German Fertighaus makers via FOCUS Money/ServiceValue fairness survey (14, standing) and DFH (massa haus, allkauf, OKAL, EinSteinHaus); Japanese kominka/machiya regeneration builders honoured by the JMRA Minka Regeneration Encouragement Prize (10, quality: Araki Komuten built 11 of the 18 honoured 2025 houses); Muji houses (Good Design BEST 100 2014 and 2020, Long Life Design Award 2015); BoKlok, Plant Prefab, Vipp Shelter (Dwell); India top 10 by FY26 bookings (PTI); China CRIC top 10 2023 plus Evergrande; France Innovapresse developer ranking (13, via Nexity's page: dated c.2021 edition); Dubai top developers 2025 (13, Arabian Business/DXBinteract); Brazil most valuable construction brands 2025 (5, InfoMoney/TM20, ISO 10668); Korean apartment brands (Raemian own Wikipedia article, NCSI No.1 since 2000; Xi, Prugio, Hillstate, e-Pyeonhan Sesang, Acro, Lotte Castle, The H, Hanwha Forena via Korea JoongAng Daily); branded residences (hotel and non-hotel, 25); HIA-CSR Australian Housing Awards 2025 winners (15 judged + 1 people's choice); NAHB Best in American Living 2025 (4, incl. REGIONS ADDED: Japan kominka/machiya regeneration (makers shown; the prize page does not itself state renown: verifier needs an independent renown quote); Seattle floating homes (Seattle Times: 'Sleepless in Seattle' made the city's floating homes 'globally famous'); Dubai branded residences (Savills: 'the hottest of hotspots for branded residences'); South Korea branded apartment complexes (JoongAng Daily: brand 'symbolizes a person's status').
THIN AREAS RETRIED: prefab/kit (Muji, BoKlok, Plant Prefab, Vipp, German Fertighaus panel added; Baufritz, Huf Haus, Honka, Clayton, Lindal, Tumbleweed, Champion Homes (formerly Skyline Champion) are already in the register; Pan-Abode found only on its own sites and LinkedIn: not added); floating homes (Seattle added; Netherlands: Waterstudio already in register, no new Dutch builder page found; Barkmet (Czech houseboats) own site only, not added); traditions (kominka added; Mongolian ger one own-site maker; Norway: only a Tracxn directory row for Nore Laft (not added); Moroccan riad restorers and Swiss chalet builders beyond Freidig: no independent page found in this pass); Good Design Award housing (Muji added; Sekisui House etc. already in register); regional rankings: Germany, France, India, China, Brazil, Gulf done; Canada beyond Mattamy/Minto/Brookfield not found on a ranking page (RevenueBase directory only). Burial places: only Forest Lawn (own site).
REGIONS NOT QUOTAS: homebuilding is national-market and volume-led; Latin America beyond Brazil, Africa, Southeast Asia, Central Asia searched only through the regional-ranking pass (nothing fetched): not counted as omissions.
MAIN BLIND SPOTS: (1) the quality layer is thin outside the UK/US/Australia juried awards and the Japanese minka prize: no juried award winners yet for Germany (Capital Fertighaus-Kompass, TUV-tested, named only Fingerhut Haus, Massa Haus, Rensch-Haus, Schwabenhaus, Danhaus in excerpt), France (Pyramides d'Argent), China, India; (2) earlier WhatHouse/Housebuilder Awards years still unfetched; (3) traditional builders (Norwegian lafting, Swiss chalet, Moroccan riad, Indian haveli) still lack independent pages; (4) estate agents are a Western luxury list (no Asian/Latin agencies); (5) burial-place sellers almost absent.
